claim.summary: Saving monotonicity: over any field, for subspaces A_i of B_i in a finite-dimensional V (i = 1..M), s(B) <= s(A), where s(A) = sum_i codim A_i - codim of the intersection (for M = 2, s(A) = codim(A_1 + A_2)). Consequently, for a degree-D PC closure C, any subspace H inside C, errors E_i of degree <= D-K and representatives E_i' with E_i - E_i' in C of degree <= D-K, the saving (summed ranks minus stacked rank) of the multiplication maps V_K -> V_D/C is at most s of the spaces Ann_H(E_i') cap V_K + C cap V_K, hence at most s of the spaces Ann_H(E_i') cap V_K, for every choice of representatives. Proof: enlarging one space by delta lowers its codimension by delta and the intersection's by at most delta.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer, who also supplied its general form (H any subspace, representatives of degree <= D-K).

claim.summary: For a finite-dimensional subspace U of a commutative ring R over a field and r(I)=dim U-dim(U cap I): r is antitone, r(I cap J)<=r(I)+r(J)-r(I+J), the stacked restriction to ideals I_1..I_M has rank r(cap I_a)<=sum r(I_a)-sum_{a>=2} r(I_a+I_b(a)) for any b(a)<a, and if each I_a contains one of K_1..K_C the joint rank is at most sum_c r(K_c). Increments r_U(I)-r_U(I+J) are monotone in U; for ideals generated by affine spans S_a,S_b in K[x_1..x_v] with 1 not in S_a+S_b, d_a=v-dim S_a and c=dim(S_a+S_b)-dim S_a, the increment for U inside degree<=k is at most c*binom(d_a+k-1,k-1). Elementary; no exactness hypothesis.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with its follow-up check, including the increment form. Submodularity is standard; ideals are generated by affine spans, so restriction is ordinary substitution.

claim.summary: Over any field F, for a finite set X in F^n, B_D the polynomials of degree <=D vanishing on X, U=V_K/(B_D cap V_K) and errors E_1..E_s of degree <=e with K+e<=D: the map u->[E_j u] in V_D/B_D has rank dim U|_{S_j}, S_j the support of E_j on X, and the stacked map has rank dim U|_S, S the union of the supports; the restriction U|_S -> direct sum of U|_{S_j} is injective, so the sum of ranks exceeds the stacked rank by its cokernel dimension. claim.summary: Over any field, let C be a degree-D PC closure, w_1..w_r of degrees e_i<=e, Ann_K(w)={u in V_K: wu in C}, and s=sum_i a_i w_i with deg a_i+e_i<=K', deg s<=sigma, s w_i - w_i in C for every i, K+K'<=D and K+sigma+e<=D. Then intersection_i Ann_K(w_i)=Ann_K(s): the common kernel of the factor maps is one annihilator. Errors E_nu=h_nu w_{i(nu)}+(member) with deg h_nu<=g and K+e+g<=D have that common kernel inside theirs. In a domain model on a finite X with 0/1-valued w_i, s=1-prod(1-w_i) qualifies when K+(r+1)e<=D; for the pigeonhole hole axioms, w_i=x_ij (i in I) and s=sum_{i in I} x_ij qualify when K+2<=D.
